notes.content:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/8b7ebab1219367bbaba69ade783d0781b1a4a048.png

TOBOR is an experimental story-based surveillance simulation game where the player plays as Tobor, a spy robot of RA Corporation, and explore ‘Undercroft’ using a surveillance system. Depending on the many choices that the player makes, players can enjoy not only changing the story inside the surveillance feeds, but also experience multiple endings.

The game was inspired by New York experimental theatre “Sleep No More”.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/1c45ee1cbb91c9dd6269a0abaf6baa3aafb0a3a1.png

While the objective of Tobor is to observe the inhabitants, there is much revealed along the way of what connections undercroft has with a character named Dr. Goralini. The gamer gathers intelligence by eavesdropping and scanning objects and uses their wits to make choices throughout the game leading to a different ending. The player is given 6 days to accomplish their given mission. The official release will reveal all the endings of the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/dca974c56006e227ef289708152d729204429e24.png

- Single Player 2D surveillance simulation game 
- A compelling tragic story with 5 characters to follow
- Investigate to find out the truth about ‘Undercroft’ 
- Observe 16 camera feeds that run simultaneously
- Learn to use the surveillance system to eavesdrop, scan objects and gather intelligence
- Find out the truth behind the weird dreams that become a reality
- Be careful on the choices you make as it will change the story
- Choices Matter game with multiple endings
- Language support available for English, Korean

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/5e3fcdc0843da9553695d3693ce9fb90953054b1.png

- Observe LIVE FEEDS of FIVE SUBJECTS
- All the subjects have their own background story and personality
- They all react differently to the same event that occurs in the same space
- Replay the game to see the different perspectives

notes.title: [TOBOR] Demo Update (v.0.6.10)
notes.content:
[PATCH NOTE]

v.0.6.10 Build Update (Aug 8, 2023)

- New Intro Cinematics
We've got a lot of feedback that the old intro didn't give a sense of what was happening, so we've basically redone it! Check! 

- Enhanced Onboarding Experience
We've noticed that many players had difficulties in understanding how the game works early on, especially with changing channels and also turning on the TV broadcast run by Stella. Hence, we've made improvements to facilitate the early game experience with better elaborations of the basic controls.  Check! 

- Separating Spy Journal & Spy Manual(Tutorial)
We've noticed that we had too much information in the file folder. Pretty much everyone skipped through it. So, we've taken measures to separate it into a Spy Journal and a Spy tutorial. The Spy Journal will keep track of the activities the player experiences as a log. The Spy Manual will focus more on learning how to use the surveillance system with simple instructions of the short-keys that will help you learn the game early on. This way, we hope that players can hop on and focus on your mission as a spy. Check.

- New Mechanism for Interventions
We've created a new puzzle game for those instances where you can interfere with the events inside the surveillance camera. During these moments of intervention, now the player can explore the actual rooms with a lot more to click and solve. Check. 

- Improved Storytelling
We've taken actions to improve the storytelling inside the surveillance camera. We noticed that there was just too much information for the player to digest while the feeds were running simultaneously, so we've made it easier for you to distinguish between the information that is important and the information that can be disregarded. This includes improved text dialogs, scan objects and the keywords associated with the information that is required to derive conclusions you want to report back to HQ. Check. 

- VO's
Finally, we had the time to implement the VO's played by amazing actors and actresses. We are really happy how the voices make the game more interactive and way more fun to play delivering so much more concept and vibe. You'll get a better feel of the characters like the contact, phone calls and Stella's morning news! Check.

- Of Course, Minor Bug Fixes! 
We've fixed minor bugs, including camera issues, SFX, and animations. 

Please take a moment to play our demo again, and let us know what you think!

Visit our Youtube to see more dev videos of TOBOR.

notes.title: Dev Log #5 Nuances of Tobor Game Development Process
notes.content:
Howdy! This is Sangpil, Executive Producer of Tobor, and you are watching 'Hotline Tobor' on CH 2. 

We just finished Steam Next Fest, and we had many players enjoy our Demo. Throughout the Next Fest we received many support and also productive feedback on how to improve the game. Thank you so much for the support!

I recently had the privilege to talk to a game media called MultiPlatform and I shared the development story behind our upcoming game Tobor. Today I wanted to take the time to share it with you. 

FRESH IDEA

Tobor was initially inspired by a New York Broadway play called Sleep No More. We loved its experimental idea where the audience can walk around a mansion and choose where to be, eventually choosing what part of the story they will experience while the whole play runs on a huge mansion with many rooms. We immediately thought it would be cool to bring this experience to gaming, and we wanted to add interactions that could make the gaming experience even more unique. 

Frankly, we've never seen a game that does this. So we had to simulate and redesign the production process, laying out all the problems we would need to solve to make this a great game experience. 

We knew that making the whole environment into a mansion like Sleep No More would be costly. We needed to add many fantasy aspects to implement the interactions where the player can change the story leading to multiple endings. We started searching for ways to solve this problem, and we were inspired by Do Not Feed the Monkeys with the core mechanics of watching a surveillance camera. 

As game developers, one of the biggest choices we had to make was dividing the venue between where the player was watching outside the surveillance camera and where all the characters played their roles inside the camera. By our definition, the interactions had to be the actions that the player takes to interfere with the events that occur inside the camera and the events inside the camera to affect the welfare of the player outside the camera.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/b4840596dfb9d97d4291977133f548a2d371a517.png

ENGAGING STORY

What we think is really cool with Tobor's storytelling is that all the characters that appear in the game (we call them The Cast) have independent stories. When all these characters walk around and interact within the story, they experience common events, but they all have different perspectives on those same events. 

Rather than following the common approach of focusing on a single protagonist, the team decided to make an ensemble cast featuring multiple principal actors who offer diverse perspectives on the central event in the story.

Trying to put the unique storytelling aspects together, we've designed it so that the player's choices eventually change the outcome of the ending, drawing in the player experience from just watching to being part of the whole story. 

Another goal we had was limiting the screens that the player can see at one time, while the whole story runs simultaneously. We wanted to limit this because there was just too much information that the player would have to digest if they were expected to follow the whole story. 

There are 16 surveillance screens in Tobor, though the player can only see one screen at a time and needs to choose which character or event they want to follow.

On the other hand, we think this experience adds a lot of replay value to the player. At the end of the day, we've created a game where the player can replay the game more than eight times, and there will still be interesting stories they can discover throughout the way. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/63bc64def5ad5c862902238c29c2de1a94aab019.png

CHOICE-BASED GAMEPLAY 

Players can make a lot of choices in Tobor. They can choose which characters to follow, which screens to watch, which character to help out, which intelligence to report back to HQ, which items to scan, which dialogues to collect, and which routes to take during the nightmares. 

On all the choices that the players can make, we've added description and story telling as much as possible. For example, the scan objects are used to tell a lot of the background history of the venue Undercroft and the founders. 

Ultimately, because the player is making all these choices, we believe the player will be able to assimilate oneself with our Tobor character playing a spy robot for RA Corporation. What's more interesting is that, as the player gradually understands more of the story will affect these choices. For example, depending on the story you've experienced, the player would have to choose whether to betray the Spy agency or not.

GRAPHICS 

The visual part was a hard one. As a small team of 6 people, we have two graphic artists and one person that does all the FX and animation. So we definitely had to find a middle ground when designing the concept art of this game. 

Overall, the most difficult problem we had to solve was dividing the visual concepts of what's real and what's a dream. As for what's real, we tried to make it dark and realistic enough to show the details when watching a surveillance camera. For the dreams and nightmares, we tried to make them look psychedelic and weird using a lot more vibrant colors. 

The game eventually progresses, where the player can't tell what's real and what's a dream. From a certain point into the game, these two very different art styles mix to create a unique experience.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/9a922dc5b77cb86bbfde7934599f8580ee4e3272.gif

The artists' goal while working on the game was to make the player feel as if they are having a blurry nightmare. 

"I imagined that these dreams would be filled with situations that don't make any sense, such as unrealistic objects and physics. Moreover, I wanted to express the unexpected connections between different spaces including sudden chases by weird monsters etc", — shares the artist Noir Dochi, the graphic artist at Tobor. 

The work of Tobor's team is all about constant communication and collaboration. While working on the graphics, the artists usually invite the animators and visual effects team to discuss how all the puzzles will match depending on the goal. They discuss all the details and steps which are necessary to create before handing the baton to the programmers. 

After the completion of the raw art sssets, the next step is to deliver them along with comprehensive guidelines for their implementation. 

Tobor, being a 2D game, requires most of the raw assets to be directly implemented in the code. During creation of these assets, it is essential to divide them into appropriate layers and components that can be efficiently incorporated into the game without delay. It is crucial for the artist to have a clear visualization and plan for these components before creating them, as this saves time. 

IMMERSIVE SOUND

The main theme song in Tobor feels lonely and dark to help the players imagine themselves alone in an abandoned research facility, trying to focus on the given mission with a strong desire to get out. 

"Sure, I've proceeded the song in minor melody using instruments like an organ and a piano to emphasize the loneliness in the music, — says Navi Nail, responsible for the music in the game. — Also, I've maximized the use of reverb and cut-off sequences to express the darkness and the tragic atmosphere at the bottom of the sea."  

Conclusion
Hope this can help players understand the problems we are tackling every day in the development process of Tobor. Please feel free to leave any questions on the comments. 

Thanks for taking your time to watch this episode and hope to see you all in another dev log episode. 

Cheers, 

Sincerely, 

Sangpil

notes.title: Dev Log #4 How the Tobor team works together to achieve the visual goals
notes.content:
Hello! This is Noir, Game Graphic Artist of Tobor, and you are watching 'Noir Dochi' on CH 1.

As an artist, I had to ask myself 'what would interest the players?', and I've decided to share the ‘small steps we take’in order to implement the art of Tobor.

I believe that the main difference between an illustrator and and game graphic artist is the level of collaboration with different parts. For example, since I can't do programming myself, I need to collaborate with a programmer to implement the art style. Collaborations is actually the toughest, but the coolest part of making games. On this devlog, I'd like to give you a brief overview of how the Tobor team works together to achieve the visuals goals.




In Tobor, classic ‘Text Adventure’games are used to make the player simulate as if they are having a dream. TAs are a great example to explain the level of collaboration while making games.

Our goal on the Text Adventure game was to “make the player feel as if they are having a blurry nightmare”. I imagined that these dreams would be filled with situations that don't make any sense, such as unrealistic objects and physics. Moreover, I wanted to express the unexpected connections between different spaces including sudden chases by weird monsters and etc. These Text Adventure visual concepts were largely inspired by the works of Satoshi Kon and Jan Svankmajer, so we have recurring dreams within dreams including a mixture of reality a dream and much more. But I'll stop here with the concepts since it could be a spoiler.



First, Ginger, the director, the team discusses the basic framework of the Text Adventure nailing down our goal, and then I start putting flesh on it for art work. Throughout the process, various changes and alterations occur and it's important to check if everyone is looking towards the same direction. Below is an example of how we add flesh to the bones articulating the visual direction of the game.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/965de713785cad5bf40755919d68210d5f52fae8.jpg



When the team is sure that everyone is on the same page, the next step is adding creativity to the directions articulated and organized in text and ultimately turning them into visual art. During this sequence, it's not only the graphic artists that get together to decide on the flesh. Instead, we also invite the animators and visual effects team to discuss how the puzzles will match depending on what to goal is. At this point we try to discuss all the details and steps necessary to create before we hand the baton to the programmers.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/20baa41fd102f52f2c6886961a617cb7624dbda5.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/87b2a8ff0830ca559069a824d9310cdad5734164.png
Finished Art graphics



Once the raw art assets are completed, It's time to deliver the assets along with detailed guidelines on how to implement them. Tobor is a 2D game, so most of the raw assets are directly implemented on the code. When creating the raw assets, we divide them into proper layers  and components that can be efficiently implemented in the game right away. In order to save time, the artist has to be able to visualize the components and plan them out before actually making them. Or else, it would take additional time to divide them after the job is done which is like redoing the work once again.
All the assets are organized so that the programmer 'Gogi' and easily tell which asset goes where.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/a36de94eed83368657158c222ac989a57f6e1d7c.png
Assets look like this when organized into little components
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/9ee59170991451d1df950e640f5cf6a8a3f20af2.gif
If necessary, the artist is animates these components to facilitate communication



Once the art assets are properly delivered and communicated to the programmer, the programmer does the magic using code, shaders and post processing which seem quite incomprehensible to a visual graphic artist. During this process, GOGI considers possible ways to implement them on the code adding feedback and discussing what could be more efficient than the other. At the end of the day, the team discusses how to improve the user experience inside the game too.

After the programmer finishes the magic, everyone gets together to discuss and verify if everything is working as it was planned. The final meetings requires a lot of attention to details.

So, this process is repeated until all the Text Adventures are implemented within the game.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/9a922dc5b77cb86bbfde7934599f8580ee4e3272.gif


Today I tried to share the process we take to discuss and to create the art of Tobor. It's important to accentuate that it is not only the art that matters when you are creating a game. It's basically designing the whole process of collaboration within the team to tackle the small and big problems we face when developing a game.
Thanks for taking your time to watch this 'Noir Dochi episode on Channel 1. Hope to see you all in another episode.

Cheers,

Sincerely,

Dochi, Game Graphic Artist

notes.title: Dev Log #2 Character and Story
notes.content:
Hello! This is GINGER , Game Director of Tobor, and you are watching 'Hotline Tobor' on CH 7.

Before we begin our show, I just want to let you know that  today's post will be more enjoyable for players who have played Rocco's island. So let's go right ahead and begin our episode of 'Hotline Tobor'.


INTRO

On our previous episode, ‘The IT Crown’, we briefly showed how TOBO all started and how it evolved over time.
On this 'Hotline Tobor' episode,  I would like to share more details about the 'Characters' and the 'Story'.

Ultimately, the team wishes to design a 'Universe' through the games we make. And when you are trying to create a 'Universe', the story and the characters are the most important asset. So during pre-production stage we had long meetings to define the pillars of the story. We ended up with three keywords.

Ensemble Cast/Failed Clones/Tragedy

I'm sure you have already noticed that they are all related to the story composition, characters and genre. After we have decided on these important pillars to create a unique game, let's dive a little deeper with the details.



Ensemble Cast

Instead of the popular model which gives precedence to a sole protagonist, we decided to make it into an ensemble cast composed of multiple principle actors that provide different angles to the same major event in the story. Believe me, writing a story in this manner was way more difficult than we ever anticipated.

We knew that we wanted to make a game that can utilize a surveillance camera with many simultaneous events happening at the same time. Using this surveillance camera system, multiple characters can move around in multiple spaces. At this point we had two possible ways to tell the story. Omnibus vs Ensemble Cast.

But why ensemble cast over omnibus?
The omnibus way would tell the stories of multiple characters independently. Each character would have their own story, but their stories would not have connections with the story of other characters. Each screen would tell a different story. However, we wanted all these individual stories and the character's past to be connected to each other formulating an environment where every character would have different perspectives to the same events that happen this world. So whichever character's story you decide to follow, you get to watch another character too and you get to a different perspective, making it a really compelling story and concept. Hence we decided to go with ensemble cast. And because there are 16 surveillance screens and because the player can only see 1 screen at a time, the player needs to chose which character or event they want to follow.

This is where 'Rocco's Island' comes in. As soon as we fixed on the ensemble cast method of storytelling, we immediately asked ourselves 'How are we going create a past to all these characters?'. We looked at Rocco's Island, and there she was, a character with a long history. Her name is 'Goralini'.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/f1ae722178b0d7f86fd9c5c142cad024d5012301.jpg
The Founder of Trillian Academy and Goralini Foundation.


Failed Clones

In Rocco's Island, Goralini creates clones. My first impression of it was that cloning human beings would be forbidden by law, and that the technology she created is probably tremendously difficult to make. Then I started to imagine that there must have been a lot experiments to create such a technology and that she probably had failed a lot too. Not to mention that wherever these experiments were done, it had to be hidden somewhere. So I concluded that there had to be 'failed clones' somewhere in the early days and started writing the plot about the many failed clones of Goralini.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/dc5b93dd466ad6bd6c94c66dc4bb1f276199f531.png
Failed Clones of Eva in Rocco's Island.

I didn't think Goralini would discard her clones just because they are failures. Moreover, even if they are experimentally considered as failures, they were humans too, not monsters. So the dev team ended up setting the characteristics of the characters as 'having mental problems' with apparent deformation of the physical body.  That's the reason why all the characters in the game are distorted or slightly awkward in different ways.

However, not all the characters in TOBOR are failed clones. Some were born in Undercroft and some where not. So we brought in other characters and designed it so that it would also have a historical connection with 'Goralini'. Whether they are clones or not, we wanted our characters to share a commonality of  'Failure' and 'Defect' throughout the game. That's why Tobor experiences a lot of failures in the game, and the story is also about characters with flawed personalities. So let me give you an example of all this through a characters named  'Maja'.



Maja- The Queen of Undercroft

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/8500f49136541edc2957c7ade1b1f110a9de9db4.png
Initial Concept Drawing of Maja

Maja  is an arrogant queen who uses her unknown powers to rule Undercroft in a very demanding way. In order to design the concept art of Maja, we tried different styles of a tyrant, cobra, judge and a ruler.  Ultimately, we decided that the concept in the middle that looks like a cobra would blend in with the story the most. We tried to use as much sharp edges to express her sharp personality.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/182c4af38fb45fa0ba8d75ac285ddc9233f3aa02.png


We developed it further and finalized it with more details. Then we turned them into graphic assets and implemented it in the game. Then we naturally moved on to the next task, which was defining her movement and animation. But before we could define her movement, we needed to define what she does and what she says. Hence, with all this under consideration, I've started to jot down about her past history, trauma and experiences to fill in the gap. Her verbal tone(mostly always strict and angry) would be all related to her past defining her current attitude and personality.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/445649283ff8f6ac4e01c8e040fe72f9a5582646.png


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/612985876dd4c1616fe66edb2c2c89eb80a2c2f6.png


Every character that appears in Tobor would all have their own versions of this settings. The majority of all this work would not be directly implemented in the game, but they were necessary settings to have everyone in the team to discuss and understand the foundations of the entire story. With all this set, I started to fill in out other gaps and settings that would be necessary to run the game play such as objects placed and minor events and dialogues. Based on these individual settings, I started to connect the characters with the major plot and story of the game. Gradually asking myself and imagining "How would this characters react in these occasions?". 


Animating

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/d12f46e2139288c000fc875c43dc559bf2ed1541.gif


We wanted to create a great 'experience'. Using text and visual art alone is not enough to to create an experience. Animating is very important. The goal is to create characters that looks live enough so that the player can assimilate into the story. While a character's appearance and dialogue may express who this character is to some extent, we believe that non-verbal character behaviors is even more powerful. Imagine a situation when the dialogue is very demanding and strong, but  the movements are timid and unstable, then the player naturally picks up that there is something wrong with this and develops more curiosity.

Well, that's one failed clone and many more to go. So repeating this process 5 more times and voila! All our main characters are complete! Then I had to use a timeline to coordinate all the information and carefully align them so that there would not have errors in the settings and storytelling. Our characters all live in a harsh environment, they all have weird personalities, what's next?


Tragedy

Oh, did I already mention that Tobor is all about tragedy? I'm sure you already know this, but Tobor is a multi-ending game and a choices matter game. All the endings will be completely different and depending on the ending, the subject of the tragic event changes. False beliefs, ignorance, excessive greed... they all are great ingredients to make a tragedy work. At least, that's how we did it. Ultimately, it's up to you to choose which tragedy is best for Tobor, because his destiny is also in your hands. We call it destiny, since in some occasions, you won't be able to control it either. I mean Tobor is the main protagonist of this tragedy after all, right?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/9ecdba8a79b7343d067b44688ff17cccbcad5aa9.gif



Conclusion

Hope you now understand how we tried to stick to ensemble cast, failed clones and tragedy. Also, we tried hard to mix these together to create a very unique game that has great replay value. Yes, you'll probably have to play it many times to understand the entire story. We've learned so much making Tobor.  Thanks to this experience, I now know how difficult it is to make great story games. Writing the scenario, designing the characters, punching out the dialogues to deliver a great gaming experience is extremely challenging. We hope it's worth it. We hope many players enjoy playing Tobor.

Thanks for taking your time to watch this 'Hotline Tobor' episode. Hope to see you all in another episode.

Cheers,

Sincerely,

Ginger, Director of Tobor.

notes.title: Dev Log #1 How TOBOR started and how it has evolved to the game it is today
notes.content:
Hello All,

This is Hyemin and you are watching 'The IT Crown' on Channel 4. 

lead programmer in team Cogoo, 
 

TOBOR is a game where you observe your subjects using a surveillance camera.

As you learn how to use the surveillance system, you not only be able to watch the many unique characters in undercroft, but also gather information by scanning objects and listening in on conversations. You might have to fix the surveillance system in case of malfunction and most importantly, you will have to connect the dots to understand the weird events that occur in the facility. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/4713cfeda29c8e6255298061ba0533c1067ad2c1.gif

On this devlog, I wanted to introduce to you the story of how it started and how it has evolved to the game it is today. 


HOW CAN WE CREATE A UNIVERSE THAT EVERYONE WANTS TO BE PART OF?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/7f20cf53a0d636f1b7d381b5bef26662d2668465.png

It all started with our previous game Rocco's Island: Ring to End the Pain which are events that occur 30,000 years to the future. In TOBOR, we come back to the 21st century and tell the story of the world after Goralini passes away. Naturally, we wanted to elaborate and provide more information on Goralini, her scientific achievements, her hidden magic and so much more. 

"Let's make a game where the player gets employed to Goralini Foundation as a new employee and gradually overcomes challenges to learn more about Goralini and her work."
The sentence is how it all started. 

As we were trying to make the process of collecting and gathering information within the game to be more fun, one thing we didn't want to do is repeat the mistake we made with Rocco's Island, a linear progression of the story meeting on character after another. Suddenly one of our artists said, "What if we can implement a different way of storytelling like that of Broadway show 'Sleep No More', that would be really interesting". We immediately thought that the idea of all the characters could have individual stories combined with the idea of a surveillance camera would be something really new. As we imagined, the players would have to choose and focus on a certain character and the only way to see the whole story would be to replay it again and again. Most importantly, we thought it would be really fun cause every player would get to see a different story. How awesome is that? 

However, there were growing concerns within the team because we've never seen a game like this before. It was very difficult to imagine what kinds of problems we would have to run into moving forward. 


Q. BUT IS IT REALLY FUN?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/f1597d8b3684fe95f408e42143efb85f8777270f.gif

This is the process we took to prove two major fun factors of the game. 

Surveillance Camera ( Every room has a different event & Story, players have to choose which camera to watch).
Gathering information and eavesdropping on conversations.

The conclusion to the prototype was clear. "This is fun!"

It was a very relieving moment since our ideas took the first step to becoming real. 

Point of interest: We tried many different art styles to get an idea on the visual direction. 

The first surveillance camera is a form in which four of the sixteen screens are placed horizontally under the enlarged screen. It was designed so that you can switch screens quickly with just a mouse click, and even when you are looking at an enlarged screen, you can get a rough idea of what is happening on the other screen.
Many different art styles were experimented. We plan on having another devlog with more details on this.


Q. Different rooms, different characters, different events. Can we design this?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/0dbbf18f929b74792bb9561304f1e0027970cdb9.gif

Since it was a spy simulator game using a surveillance camera, we knew that it had to be 'fun to watch'. 

Therefore, even from the game design phase, we tried many different background colors and many different character styles.

In order to determine whether we can implement the characters that were mere imaginations in our heads, we simply created characters and backgrounds, and divided and organized the compositions that can be expressed in 2D games. 


MOVEMENT OF ACTORS IN SPACE

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/00167a960b6919e2d5451d387890200448b2e26e.gif

Everything slowly started to come together. We were starting to build more confidence since the background theme, characters and movement were visual. Hence, it was time for the team to make things look more real and lively. 

We focused on making the movements as natural, controlling the speed and sound according to the storyboard. 

This is the first moment that the characters are not just sprites, but moving characters within the surveillance camera. 

Point of Interest: New Surveillance Camera design and information scanner
You can see that when a screen is selected and enlarged, the other screens are hidden so that the player can focus only on the selected screen.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/abb5f01d4a1769321d9b497074badc220dd5daf9.gif
The information scanners initially looked like credit cards. We thought that bringing the fun of purchasing something using a credit card would be really interesting since everyone loves shopping. 


ONE STEP AFTER ANOTHER

We now had a more clear idea of what the game would look like and why it would be fun playing it. We were prepared to move on to the next step. We had to write and set up the story of characters along with the environments, practically write a play and conversation dialogues, design the interactions and the events that the characters would deliver when they meet each other. Repeating this design process again and again to build the world inside the surveillance camera. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42658268/6c611e6b9a6ab91188b04fde1d49497de30e4068.jpg

The system is off right now, but once it gets turned on, the world we designed will unfold before your eyes. 

Stay tuned for more devlog stories of TOBOR.
